speaker: margery_pell
text: Four shillings and tenpence, and I'd have given them their pennies back to go home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: How many bodies did the four and tenpence buy?

speaker: margery_pell
text: Some sixty souls, and a few wet gowns. I counted the gowns by the drip on my stair, and the souls by the pennies. Do not ask me to call it a house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It was billed. It is played. It is the last at this house for the year.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Then the year may end. I am wringing a sleeve into the yard, and the sleeve is not mine.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Leave the sleeve, Margery. I have a better wetness. From Somerset House, by a man who does not drip.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The Queen has put off her going to Richmond for the weather, until tomorrow. Item, she has sense. The tilt-boat stands.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tomorrow. Not at all, and not Friday's ice. Tomorrow.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Tomorrow. Gannet's Wednesday still serves. I will not enter a second deposit, and I will not enter a share off four shillings and tenpence.

speaker: margery_pell
text: You will not enter my four and tenpence as a triumph, either. Sixty souls. I have said it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sixty, and the last. Both heels in the morning, John?

speaker: john_heminges
text: Both heels in the morning. Hose, baskets, and the order of going. Today is done. God keep you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And you. The walk home is into the wind. I will take it, and I will not count anything at the end of it.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Count the drips if you like. They are free.
